title: Are We Overestimating Cryo-ET? Evaluating the Role of 2D Cryo-EM for In Situ Studies
content: The rapid advancement of structural biology in recent years—particularly in cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM), which now achieves near-atomic resolution (∼1 Å) [1,2]—has been remarkable. Coupled with improvements in protein structure prediction [3], we are now in a position where 3D structures have been experimentally determined, or can be confidently predicted, for a significant portion of the proteome. Consequently, efforts are now shifting from determining the structures of isolated macromolecules to understanding their complex interplay within cells.
